channel.title: Jeep recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee and Wagoneer Tire Warning Light May Fail
item.description: A software error means the tire pressure system may not spot a low tire, and the low-pressure warning light on your dash may not come on when it should. You could drive on an underinflated tire without knowing, which makes the vehicle harder to control and raises the chance of a crash. The fix is a free software update at the dealer. Owner letters are expected to start going out September 29, 2026; until then, check your tire pressures yourself with a gauge.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee rear springs can fall off
item.description: The rear coil springs are the big metal springs that hold up the back of your Jeep and soak up bumps. On these vehicles they may have been installed incorrectly at the factory, and a spring can work loose and come off the vehicle while you are driving. Chrysler is replacing the rubber pads the springs sit on. The final fix is not ready yet, so owners are getting a warning letter first and a second letter later.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee and Wagoneer gear display may vanish
item.description: Certain Jeep Grand Cherokee, Grand Cherokee L, Wagoneer and Wagoneer L vehicles have a software error that can stop the gear display from showing. That is the readout that tells you whether the vehicle is in park, reverse, neutral or drive. Without it, you cannot confirm the vehicle is actually in park before you step out, and it may move when you do not expect it or roll away on its own. Dealers reprogram the shifter software for free.

item.title: Jeep Wrangler and Gladiator Power Steering Wiring Fire Risk
item.description: The wiring that feeds the electric power steering pump can overheat. That overheating can start a fire in the vehicle, and it can happen even when the Jeep is parked with the ignition switched off — so shutting it down does not make it safe. A dealer will inspect the wiring and the power steering pump and replace either part if needed, at no cost. Owner notification letters are expected to go out July 9, 2026.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee side airbags may deploy too late
item.description: A software mistake in the computer that controls the airbags and seat belts can delay the side airbags during a crash. The airbags still go off, but not as quickly as they should, so they may not be fully in place when you need them. Because of this, these Jeeps do not meet the federal side-impact protection rule. The fix is a free software update at the dealer. Your VIN becomes searchable on NHTSA's website on May 28, 2026.

item.title: Jeep Cherokee power transfer unit can fail, causing rollaway
item.description: The part that sends power to the wheels, called the power transfer unit, can break on certain Jeep Cherokees. If it fails, the vehicle may suddenly lose the ability to move under its own power, or it may roll away on its own even when you think it is parked. Chrysler is still finalizing the full fix. Dealers will update the drivetrain and electronic parking brake software, and replace the power transfer unit if needed, at no cost.

item.title: Dodge Charger EV and Jeep Wagoneer S display failure
item.description: A software error can make the main display screen behind the steering wheel fail. That screen is what tells you which gear the car is in and shows warning lights for the brakes, tire pressure, stability control, and airbags. If it goes blank, you could miss an important warning or not know whether the car is in drive or reverse. A dealer reloads the display software during a normal service visit.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer S liftgate hinge cover may fall off
item.description: On these Jeep Wagoneer S vehicles, the cover over the rear liftgate hinge may not have been clipped fully into place when the vehicle was built. If it works free, it can come off the vehicle while you are driving. The main danger is to people behind you — a loose piece of trim in the road can cause another driver to crash. Your dealer will inspect the cover and refit or replace it as needed, free of charge.

item.title: Jeep and Ram trailer lights and brakes may fail
item.description: The part that sends power from your vehicle to a trailer was designed wrong. If you tow, the trailer's brake lights and turn signals may not light up, so drivers behind you cannot tell when you are slowing down or turning. The trailer's own brakes can also stop working, which leaves your vehicle doing all the stopping with a heavy trailer pushing from behind. The dealer replaces the trailer tow module at no cost.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee rear coil springs may fall off
item.description: The rear coil springs are big metal springs that hold up the back of the vehicle. On these Jeeps, they may have been installed incorrectly and can come loose and fall off while you are driving. Chrysler says that raises the risk of a crash. Dealers will inspect and repair the rear spring assembly free of charge. Interim letters went out in February 2026, and the final repair was expected in March 2026, with a second letter to follow.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee 4xe engine may fail or catch fire
item.description: Leftover debris inside the engine can damage it and make the engine quit. If that happens, the vehicle can lose power while you are driving, and in some cases a fire can start under the hood. Dealers will load a software update now, and will replace the engine block or the whole engine if it is needed. Chrysler has started mailing owner letters, and more letters will go out when the full fix is ready.

item.title: Jeep Wrangler and Grand Cherokee 4xe Battery Fire Risk
item.description: The large high-voltage battery in these plug-in hybrid Jeeps can fail inside and catch fire. It can happen while you are driving or while the vehicle is parked. Until it is fixed, Jeep says park outside away from buildings and do not plug the vehicle in to charge. A dealer will update the battery software and replace the battery if needed, free of charge. Vehicles already repaired under recalls 24V720 or 23V787 still need this new repair.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer quarter window trim can come off
item.description: The trim piece at the edge of the driver's and passenger's side windows may not have been fastened down properly at the factory. Over time it can work loose and detach from the vehicle. If it comes off while you're driving, it becomes a loose object in the road that another driver could hit or swerve to avoid. The dealer inspects the area and replaces the quarter window glass assembly if it's needed.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer door trim can come off while driving
item.description: The decorative trim strips on the driver and passenger doors were not attached properly on some of these Jeeps, and they can work loose and fall off. A piece of trim lying in the road, or flying off at speed, is a hazard for the drivers behind you who have to swerve or run over it. Dealers will look at the door trim and replace it where it is needed, free of charge.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer S built with wrong dashboard support beam
item.description: Some 2025 Jeep Wagoneer S vehicles were built with the wrong support beam running across the inside of the dashboard. That beam is part of the structure that helps hold things in place and protect people up front in a crash. Because the wrong part was used, the vehicle may not protect the driver and front passenger as well as it should in a collision. Dealers will replace the beam with the correct one at no charge.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee plug-in hybrids can lose driving power
item.description: This affects Grand Cherokees with the plug-in hybrid setup, which runs on both gas and a battery. The computer that manages that hybrid system has a software error, and because of it the vehicle can suddenly lose the power that drives the wheels. That could leave you slowing down or stuck in traffic without warning. The fix is a free software update at the dealer, which takes the place of any parts replacement.

item.title: Dodge Charger and Jeep Wagoneer S electrics may roll away
item.description: In these electric vehicles, a spring inside the unit that drives the wheels may have been put in wrong. Because of that, the vehicle may not truly stay in Park when you move the gear selector to P, and it can roll away on its own. The vehicle also does not meet the federal rule meant to prevent rollaways. A dealer will replace the electric drive module at no charge to you.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee second-row headrests may not lock
item.description: The headrests on the second-row seats of these Jeep Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L models may not lock in the upright position. A headrest that will not stay up cannot support the head of the person sitting there, so passengers in that row have less protection in a crash. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule for head restraints. Dealers will inspect both second-row headrests and replace them if needed, free of charge.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee blower motor can kill defroster
item.description: The blower motor — the fan that pushes air through the vents — can fail. If it quits, the defroster and defogger stop working, so you cannot clear fog or frost from the windshield. That leaves you looking through a clouded or iced-over window, and poor visibility makes a crash more likely. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal standard for windshield defrosting and defogging. A dealer will inspect the blower motor and replace it if needed, free of charge.

item.title: Jeep Cherokee power transfer unit may fail, rollaway risk
item.description: A part called the power transfer unit, which helps send power to the wheels, can become damaged. If it breaks, it can disconnect the transmission from the differential. That means the car may lose power and stop moving while you are driving. It also means Park may not actually hold the vehicle, so the Jeep could roll away on its own after you get out. A dealer will update the software and replace the part if it needs it.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer S headlights cannot be aimed correctly
item.description: The headlights on these electric Jeep Wagoneer S SUVs cannot be aimed correctly. The opening used to adjust how high or low the beams point is blocked by a plug, and the side-to-side adjustment is left uncovered when it should be plugged. That means a shop cannot set the beams where they belong. Headlights pointed too low leave less of the road lit, and beams aimed too high shine into other drivers' eyes. A dealer moves the plugs so the aim can be set.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee backup camera screen may go blank
item.description: A small electrical part inside the big center touchscreen can get too hot, and when it does the backup camera picture doesn't come up on the screen. Backing up without that view makes it harder to see people or objects behind you, and federal rules require the image. Chrysler says dealers already replaced the display in every affected Jeep, so if yours was covered the work has been done.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer and Grand Cherokee backup camera may not show
item.description: Certain 2024 Jeep Wagoneer, Grand Wagoneer, Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L models have incorrect software in the rearview camera. Because of it, the camera picture may not appear on the screen when you shift into reverse. Without that view, you cannot see what is directly behind the vehicle while backing up. This also means these vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility rule. Dealers will reprogram the camera module with corrected software at no charge to you.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee loose radiator bolts risk airbag, fuel problems
item.description: Bolts that hold the metal support bar for the radiator at the front of these SUVs may not be tightened properly. Because of that, in a crash the airbags may not deploy the way they should, and fuel can leak. Airbags that go off incorrectly can hurt the people inside, and leaking gasoline can catch fire. The vehicles fail two federal safety standards, one for crash protection and one for fuel system integrity. Dealers will check the bolts and tighten them free of charge.

item.title: Jeep Renegade may have wrong reverse light assembly
item.description: The wrong reverse light assembly may have been installed in the rear bumper at the factory, so these vehicles do not meet the federal rules for lamps and reflectors. The result is that the backup lights may not light up the area behind the vehicle as well as they should. They also may not be noticeable enough to warn people walking behind you, or other drivers, that your Renegade is about to back up.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee side airbags may not deploy
item.description: A connector for the side airbags built into the front seats may not have been fastened properly at the factory. If that connection is loose, the side airbags might not inflate during a side-impact crash, leaving you without that protection. The airbags look normal and there is no warning you would notice while driving. The fix is simple — the dealer secures the connector at no cost. Chrysler says every affected vehicle has already been repaired.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee speedometer may show wrong speed
item.description: The screen behind the steering wheel runs on software, and an error in that software can make the speedometer show a speed that isn't your actual one. You could be traveling faster or slower than the number you see. Nothing is physically broken and the rest of the vehicle works normally, but the display fails the federal rule requiring accurate speed readings. A dealer checks the cluster and loads corrected software.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee, Dodge Durango brake module failure
item.description: A fault in the antilock brake computer can switch off both antilock braking and the stability control that keeps you from sliding in a turn. It can also make your brake lights come on when you are not braking, and it can let you start the vehicle and shift out of Park without your foot on the brake — so the vehicle could roll away. Dealers will replace a brake sensor and update the software, free. Vehicles already fixed under the earlier recall 22V-426 need this new repair too.

item.title: Jeep Wrangler and Grand Cherokee 4xe batteries can catch fire
item.description: The large battery that powers these plug-in hybrid Jeeps can fail inside and catch fire, while you are driving or even while the vehicle sits parked. Chrysler tells owners to park outside, away from buildings and other cars, and to stop plugging the vehicle in to charge until it is fixed. Dealers update the battery software and replace the battery pack if needed. A newer recall has since replaced this one, so repaired vehicles need the new fix too.

item.title: Jeep Wrangler wiring may disable camera and brake light
item.description: The wiring for the rearview camera and the center brake light — the one mounted high on the back — can short out. When that happens, the camera picture will not show when you back up, and the center brake light will not light up when you slow down, so drivers behind you may not see that you are braking. Dealers replaced the wiring, and the spare tire carrier assembly if needed, free of charge. Chrysler says all affected vehicles were repaired by January 15, 2024.

item.title: Jeep Wrangler and Gladiator Dashboard Cluster Can Short Out
item.description: The instrument cluster, the panel behind the steering wheel with your speedometer, gauges and warning lights, can short out inside and stop working. If it goes dark while you are driving, you will not see how fast you are going or any warning lights telling you something is wrong, which can lead to a crash. Because the problem is in the hardware, dealers replace the whole cluster, free of charge. Owner letters went out between October 2024 and January 2025, so the repair is available now.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee L child seat anchor welds may fail
item.description: The welds that hold the child-seat top tether anchors on the back of the second-row seat may not be strong enough. Those anchors are the hook-up points for the strap at the top of a forward-facing child seat. In a crash, weak welds could let the anchor pull loose, so the child seat would not hold the child in place the way it should. The vehicle does not meet the federal rule for child-seat anchors.

item.title: Jeep Wrangler and Gladiator engine may stall unexpectedly
item.description: Certain 2021 Jeep Wrangler and Gladiator vehicles have a software problem in the computer that controls the engine and transmission. The software can cause the engine to stall, which means you suddenly lose power to the wheels while driving. These vehicles were already fixed once under an earlier recall, but that fix was not enough — they need the new repair too. A dealer will load updated software into the powertrain control module at no cost.

item.title: Jeep Cherokee right curtain airbag connector not properly secured
item.description: The plug that connects the right-side curtain airbag was not pushed in and secured properly. That is the bag which drops down over the right-side windows in a side crash or rollover. With a loose connection, the airbag may not go off when it is needed. Because of this the vehicles do not meet the federal rules for side impact protection and for keeping people from being thrown out. A dealer secures the connector at no charge.

item.title: Jeep Renegade front airbag may not deploy in crash
item.description: A small switch in the front seat belt buckle may not be plugged in correctly. That switch tells the vehicle whether someone is buckled in, and the airbag system uses that information to decide how to fire. Because of the bad connection, the front seat airbag may not go off the way it should in a crash. Nothing warns you that the connection is wrong. A dealer will repair the connection at no cost.

item.title: Jeep, Ram, Chrysler backup camera may show nothing
item.description: The radio software in these vehicles can keep the backup camera picture from appearing at all. When you shift into reverse, the screen may not show what is behind you, so you cannot see a child, a person, or an object in the vehicle's path while backing up. That makes it much easier to hit something you never saw. The repair is a software update for the radio, done at the dealer or sent to the vehicle wirelessly.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee second-row seat belt buckle bolt loose
item.description: The buckle you click a seat belt into, for the second-row seats, is held to the vehicle by a bolt. On these Grand Cherokees, that bolt may not have been tightened enough at the factory. A buckle that is not firmly anchored may not hold a passenger in place during a crash, so someone belted into that seat could be hurt. A dealer will check the bolt and tighten it if it is loose.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee missing bumper foam affects airbag deployment
item.description: Some 2024 Jeep Grand Cherokees left the factory missing a piece of energy-absorbing foam inside the front bumper. Chrysler says that missing foam can keep the front airbags from going off the way they are supposed to in a crash, so the vehicle does not meet the federal rule for crash protection. If the airbags do not work as designed, people in the front seats face a greater chance of injury. A dealer will inspect the bumper and add the foam if needed.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee backup camera image may not appear
item.description: On some 2023 Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L SUVs, the connections behind the dashboard screen were not fastened tightly enough. When that happens, the picture from the backup camera may not appear on the screen when you shift into reverse. You lose the view of the area right behind the vehicle that the camera is there to show you, and federal rules require that image to appear. Chrysler says every affected vehicle has already been fixed.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee backup camera image may not appear
item.description: A cable behind the dashboard screen may not be plugged in all the way. When that happens, the picture from the backup camera does not show up on the screen when you shift into reverse. Without that view you cannot see people, pets, or objects directly behind the vehicle, so it is easier to back into something. The dealer simply pushes the cable connection together properly. Chrysler says every affected vehicle has already been fixed.
